subject: Renal
vignette: An intravenous urogram in a child with recurrent urinary tract infections shows two separate renal collecting systems on one side and a single ureter that splits into a Y shape before entering the bladder. The radiologist diagnoses a duplex collecting system and explains its embryologic origin to the parents.
question: Which embryologic event most directly produces the Y-shaped bifid ureter of a duplex collecting system?

options.text: Failure of the ureteropelvic junction to canalize
Fusion of the inferior poles of the two kidneys
Failure of the ureteric bud to develop
Degeneration of the mesonephric duct in a female fetus
Bifurcation of the ureteric bud before it enters the metanephric blastema

explanation_correct: A duplex collecting system can result from bifurcation of the ureteric bud before it enters the metanephric blastema, creating a Y-shaped bifid ureter; it can also arise from two separate ureteric buds reaching and interacting with the blastema. These systems are strongly associated with vesicoureteral reflux and ureteral obstruction, increasing the risk of urinary tract infections and hydronephrosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Failure of ureteropelvic junction canalization causes congenital hydronephrosis of a single system, not a duplicated collecting system with a bifid ureter.
explanation_incorrect.B: Fusion of the inferior poles produces a horseshoe kidney, in which the two kidneys are joined but each has its own collecting system rather than a bifid ureter.
explanation_incorrect.C: Failure of the ureteric bud to develop produces renal agenesis with absence of the kidney and ureter, not a duplicated system.
explanation_incorrect.D: Degeneration of the mesonephric duct in females is a normal event and does not create a bifid ureter or duplicated collecting system.

educationalObjective: A Y-shaped bifid ureter in a duplex collecting system results from bifurcation of the ureteric bud before it enters the metanephric blastema.

subject: Renal
vignette: A 6-year-old girl has had three episodes of febrile urinary tract infection in the past year. Ultrasound shows a duplicated collecting system on the right with mild dilation of the upper-pole moiety. Her pediatrician explains that this anomaly predisposes to abnormal urine flow and infection.
question: A duplex collecting system is most strongly associated with which of the following?

options.text: Horseshoe kidney with inferior pole fusion
Complete absence of the ureter on the affected side

explanation_correct: A duplex collecting system is strongly associated with vesicoureteral reflux and/or ureteral obstruction, which increase the risk of recurrent urinary tract infections. It frequently presents with hydronephrosis. In this child, the duplicated system with a dilated moiety and recurrent febrile infections fits these associations.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bilateral renal agenesis is a separate severe anomaly causing absent kidneys and Potter sequence; it is not an association of a duplex collecting system.
explanation_incorrect.C: Inferior pole fusion describes a horseshoe kidney and its entrapment under the inferior mesenteric artery, not a duplicated collecting system.
explanation_incorrect.D: Complete absence of the ureter occurs in renal agenesis; a duplex system by definition has duplicated or bifid ureteral drainage, not absent ureters.
explanation_incorrect.E: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease causes enlarged cystic kidneys and can produce Potter sequence, but it is not the association with a duplex system.

educationalObjective: Duplex collecting systems are strongly associated with vesicoureteral reflux and ureteral obstruction, leading to recurrent UTIs and hydronephrosis.

subject: Renal
vignette: An embryo is found to have two fully formed ureters on one side, each draining a separate renal pelvis and each reaching and interacting with its own region of metanephric blastema. There is no single ureter that splits into a Y. The eventual anatomy will be a duplicated collecting system with two ureters rather than a bifid one.
question: Which of the following describes this alternative mechanism by which a duplex collecting system can arise?

options.text: Two separate ureteric buds reaching and interacting with the metanephric blastema
A single ureteric bud that fails to undergo canalization
The metanephric mesenchyme splitting into two distinct blastemas
Fusion of two adjacent metanephric kidneys
Persistence of the mesonephric duct as a second ureter

explanation_correct: Besides early bifurcation of a single ureteric bud, a duplex collecting system can arise when two separate ureteric buds reach and interact with the metanephric blastema, producing two ureters and two collecting systems. Regardless of mechanism, the anomaly is associated with vesicoureteral reflux, obstruction, hydronephrosis, and increased urinary tract infection risk.

explanation_incorrect.B: A ureteric bud that fails to canalize would produce an obstructed or absent ureter, not two separate ureters draining duplicated systems.
explanation_incorrect.C: The duplicated system results from abnormal ureteric bud number or branching, not from the metanephric mesenchyme splitting into two separate blastemas.
explanation_incorrect.D: Fusion of two kidneys would produce a fused renal mass such as a horseshoe kidney, not two ureters from one renal side interacting with one blastema.
explanation_incorrect.E: Persistence of the mesonephric duct as the Wolffian duct forms male internal reproductive structures; it is not the source of a second ureter.

educationalObjective: A duplex collecting system can arise either from early bifurcation of one ureteric bud or from two ureteric buds interacting with the metanephric blastema.
